\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Hermite --- Generator: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Exponential values in the correlation interval]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exp_neg_mem_correlationInterval}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exp_neg_mem_correlationInterval}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every real number $t\ge 0$, the value $e^{-t}$ belongs to the interval $[-1,1]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian generator multiplier]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{
  pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p008-b001,
  pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p012-b001
}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier}
\leanok
For a natural number $d$ and a real number $t$, define the Gaussian generator multiplier
by $\bigl(1-e^{-dt}\bigr)/t$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Limit of the Gaussian generator multiplier]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier_tendsto}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier_tendsto}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier}
\difficulty{4}
For every integer $d\ge 0$, the Gaussian generator multiplier $m_d(t)$ tends to $d$ as
$t$ tends to $0$ through positive values.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bounds for the Gaussian generator multiplier]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier_bounds}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier_bounds}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier}
\difficulty{4}
For every integer $d\ge 0$ and every real $t>0$, the Gaussian generator multiplier
$m_d(t)$ satisfies $0\le m_d(t)\le d$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Squared multiplier error bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier_error_sq_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier_error_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier_bounds}
\difficulty{4}
For every integer $d\ge 0$, every real $t>0$, and every real $c$, the Gaussian generator
multiplier satisfies $\bigl((m_d(t)-d)c\bigr)^2\le (dc)^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Convergence of the summed multiplier error]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier_error_tsum_tendsto}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier_error_tsum_tendsto}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier_error_sq_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier_tendsto}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\iota$ be any type, and let $d_i\in\mathbb N$ and $c_i\in\mathbb R$ be indexed by
$i\in\iota$. If $\sum_{i\in\iota}(d_ic_i)^2$ is finite, then as $t$ tends to $0$ through
positive values, $\sum_{i\in\iota}\bigl((m_{d_i}(t)-d_i)c_i\bigr)^2$ tends to $0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian noise difference quotient is square-integrable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.memLp_gaussianGeneratorQuotient}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.memLp_gaussianGeneratorQuotient}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exp_neg_mem_correlationInterval, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_memLp}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belong to $L^2$ for
product standard Gaussian measure. For every $t\ge0$, the function
\[x\longmapsto \frac{f(x)-T_{e^{-t}}f(x)}{t}\]
belongs to $L^2$ for that measure, where $T_\rho f(x)$ is the average of $f(\rho
x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,y)$ over standard Gaussian $y\in\mathbb R^n$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{1}
Let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have Gaussian generator $g$. In the $L^2$ space for
the product standard Gaussian measure, the series indexed by $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$ with
terms $|\alpha|\widehat f(\alpha)H_\alpha$ sums to $g$, where
$|\alpha|=\sum_{j=1}^n\alpha_j$, $\widehat f(\alpha)$ is the Hermite coefficient of $f$,
and $H_\alpha$ is the corresponding normalized Hermite function viewed as an $L^2$
element.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian generator from Hermite coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasGaussianGenerator_of_hermiteCoeff}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasGaussianGenerator_of_hermiteCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasGaussianGenerator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_two_eq_sqrt_hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorMultiplier_error_tsum_tendsto, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_gaussianGeneratorQuotient, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_sq_summable, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_sub, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.memLp_gaussianGeneratorQuotient}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge0$, and let $f,g\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be square-integrable with
respect to the product standard Gaussian measure. Suppose that for every multi-index
$\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, the Hermite coefficient of $g$ at $\alpha$ equals $|\alpha|$
times the Hermite coefficient of $f$ at $\alpha$, where $|\alpha|=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i$.
Then $f$ has Gaussian generator $g$: both functions are square-integrable, and as
$t\to0^+$, the $L^2$ norm under product standard Gaussian measure of
$(f-P_{e^{-t}}f)/t-g$ tends to zero, where $P_\rho f(x)=\mathbb E[f(\rho
x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Y)]$ and $Y$ has product standard Gaussian law.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian generator domain and Hermite coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorDomain_iff_hermite}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianGeneratorDomain_iff_hermite}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.InGaussianGeneratorDomain, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exists_memLp_hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasGaussianGenerator_of_hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_gaussianGenerator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_sq_summable}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge 0$ and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be square-integrable with respect to
the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures. Then $f$ belongs to the domain of the
Gaussian generator if and only if the sum over all multi-indices $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$
of $|\alpha|^2\widehat f(\alpha)^2$ is finite, where $|\alpha|=\sum_{j=1}^n\alpha_j$ and
$\widehat f(\alpha)$ is the Hermite coefficient of $f$.
\end{theorem}
